item.title: Donna Mills does 100 sit-ups a day, plays tennis five times a week at 85 but won't quit Doritos

'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS REFUSING TO POSE NUDE COST HER PLAYBOY COVER

WATCH: 'Knots Landing' star Donna Mills swears by this daily routine at 85

Still, she said the popular snack has followed her throughout her decades-long career.

"Different sets that I’ve been on… for some reason, they know — they always got a bag of Doritos in the trailer for me… it’s really funny. But I’ve never lost that. I don’t eat them as much as I used to. But they’re still a treat."

When it comes to exercise, Mills' routine is considerably more demanding.

'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS ISSUES URGENT WARNING ABOUT AGING

To this day, she still incorporates elements of her early training into her workouts.

DICK VAN DYKE SHOCKS FANS BY POSTING INVERSION TABLE WORKOUT AT AGE 100

"I do 100 sit-ups a day, 50 leg lifts, lots of stretching. I have a ballet barre in my little gym."

"I’ve always been anti-sugar," she said. "I read a book a long time ago called 'Sugar Blues' that really talked about the sugar industry and everything, and I have stayed away from it ever since."

item.title: Trump negotiators Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Moscow as US pushes for end to Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have landed in Moscow for peace talks before heading to Kyiv, as Trump says there may be a good chance for a deal.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump's son-in-law and adviser, Jared Kushner, are visiting Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend in an effort to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

"We have an idea for peace," Trump told reporters on Friday. "I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it," he said.

Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelenskyy confirmed the news in a post on X.

"Today, it has been clearly established that U.S. envoys will be in Ukraine and Russia in the coming days. We have the details from the U.S. President’s team. We discussed today that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Moscow and then Kyiv on Sunday. We are preparing for the visit," Zelenskyy wrote.

TRUMP ANNOUNCES SURPRISE THREE-DAY CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

The pair will visit Russia first on Saturday and, according to Russian state-affiliated media outlet Tass, have already landed in Moscow. 

Photos showed Kushner and Witkoff greeted by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev shortly after landing in Moscow.

Kushner and Witkoff are expected to later travel to Kyiv on Sunday, Zelenskyy confirmed. Zelenskyy also said that Ukraine will work to keep Russian airspace safe during the Americans’ visit.

CIA DIRECTOR JOHN RATCLIFFE MET WITH RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICIALS IN VISIT TO MOSCOW, KREMLIN SAYS

"Just as we did during previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely. We are looking out for them, not for Russia. There will be no air strikes from our side, and Russia must do the same, ensuring there are no air strikes from its side for the time needed to hold these talks and handle the logistical matters related to this American visit," he wrote on X.

ZELENSKYY CONGRATULATES TRUMP ON TURNING 80 IN BIRTHDAY CALL, VOWS MORE UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AT G7 ON TUESDAY

"Our goal is to make the visit and the talks with the U.S. side as constructive and substantive as possible. We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end. We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response," the Ukrainian president concluded.

Zelenskyy, in a subsequent Saturday morning post on X, said he had already communicated with Witkoff and Kushner ahead of their planned Sunday meeting.

"I have just spoken with the U.S. President’s envoys. They have already begun working with the Russian side today. From the moment of this conversation, we are ready to observe a ceasefire in airstrikes against the cities involved in the negotiation process. From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv," he wrote.

"Today, I also received reports from Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapatyi on the situation at the front, the dynamics of threats in Ukraine’s airspace, our steps, and active defensive operations. I am grateful to every one of our warriors for effectively defending Ukraine’s positions," Zelenskyy's post continued. 

"On the diplomatic track, our actions must be, and will be, just as strong and effective – one hundred percent. The plan for tomorrow’s diplomatic engagements in Kyiv, involving the U.S. team, has been approved. We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation. Thank you to everyone who stands with Ukraine!" Zelenskyy concluded. 

Zelenskyy’s Friday message came the same day that a Russian drone strike targeted the Security Service of Ukraine’s headquarters in Ukraine, Zelenskyy wrote in a public message on the app Telegram.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

Zelenskyy alleged the strike directly targeted the head of the Security Service's office.

He also wrote that he was directing the head, Oleksandr Poklad, to prepare a retaliatory strike. "I gave Poklad the task of adequately, noticeably and, if possible, mirroring the Russians' response to this attack, when everything is prepared. Our military will support this response. Glory to Ukraine!" he wrote.

PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END

At least nine people were injured in the explosion, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko also wrote on Telegram.

The visit also comes just one day after German officials formally accused Russia of attempting an explosive drone attack on a major airport in Germany.

RUSSIA’S STRIKES NEAR MOLDOVA RAISE ALARM OVER PUTIN’S PLANS FOR EUROPE’S EASTERN FLANK

"The attack on the aircraft in Leipzig was concrete; it could have triggered a catastrophe had it succeeded. The attacker was, at most, covert, but even here there is now certainty: The German government has named Russia as the mastermind. Patterns of attack, police investigations, and intelligence findings prove Russian responsibility for the drone attack," Stefan Kornelius, a spokesperson for the German federal government, wrote Friday.

Fox News Digital contacted the White House and the foreign ministries for Russia, Ukraine and Germany for further comment.

item.title: Arizona voter-law fight reaches SCOTUS as election groups warn ‘absurd’ consequence could ensue
item.description: Election experts warn the Supreme Court that the Ninth Circuit's ruling could make it impossible to ever remove noncitizens from state voter rolls.
item.content:encoded:
Election experts are warning the Supreme Court that affirming a lower court's ruling could mean that noncitizens, minors, or factitious people listed on state voter rolls could be impossible to remove.

The Supreme Court is set to hear oral arguments in RNC v. Mi Familia Vote this December and will determine whether a pair of Arizona's state laws which remove the registrations of noncitizen voters from voter rolls within 90 days of the election and require voters to show proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote are in violation of the National Voter Registration Act.

"Citizenship is a qualification for voting. If states are going to enforce that requirement, they have to be able to verify it," Justin Riemer, president & CEO of Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "And when officials find noncitizens on the voter rolls, they should be able to act before an election, not after. We are confident the Supreme Court will agree and reverse the Ninth Circuit's misguided ruling."

In an amicus brief filed on Thursday, attorneys from Center for Election Confidence, Inc., Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections, Inc., and Honest Elections Project, argued that the Ninth Circuit Court's ruling that the Arizona laws are an act of "voter suppression" is "absurd" and raises serious threats to state rights.

CLINTON-APPOINTED JUDGE TRIGGERS APPEAL AFTER BLOCKING KEY VOTER CITIZENSHIP LAW

The brief argued that Congress may regulate the mechanics of federal elections, but states have the constitutional authority to set and enforce voter qualifications — a power they argued becomes meaningless if states cannot obtain documentation needed to verify citizenship or remove people who were never eligible to register.

"Since the power to establish voting requirements is of little value without the power to enforce those requirements, it would raise serious constitutional doubts if a federal statute precluded a State from obtaining the information necessary to enforce its voter qualifications," the brief stated.

The amicus brief pushed back on the Ninth Circuit’s conclusion that Arizona cannot conduct a systematic program to remove noncitizens from voter rolls during the NVRA’s 90-day pre-election period. The federal law generally requires states to complete systematic voter-removal programs at least 90 days before a federal election, while allowing removals during that window for a voter’s request, death, criminal conviction or mental incapacity.

DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED

The groups argued that non-citizenship is not among those listed grounds because it concerns someone who was never eligible to register in the first place. They said the restriction is meant to protect eligible voters from erroneous last-minute removals — not to shield people who were never eligible to register.

"If the Ninth Circuit is right that the 90-day limitation on programs prohibits removal on these bases — because the statute has listed exceptions — States could never remove improperly registered individuals who fall within these categories, no matter when the removal happens or whether it is after a systematic inquiry," the brief said.

"Not just that, but these States could never remove these noncitizens who were never eligible to vote," the brief continued.

The brief pointed to reported registration errors in New Jersey, Illinois and Oregon as examples of why states need a mechanism to correct allegedly improper registrations. It argues that an unlawful ballot cannot be undone once cast and counted.

DHS APPROVES PLAN TO VERIFY VOTER CITIZENSHIP, MONITOR MAIL BALLOTS AS TRUMP PUSH INTENSIFIES

"American elections are for American citizens only. Period," Lisa Dixon, executive director of the Center for Election Confidence, said in a statement. "We should all support Arizona ensuring non-citizens can’t register to vote and removing any non-citizens who end up on the voter lists."

The amici also argued that the Ninth Circuit misread NVRA provisions governing what information is "necessary" for state election officials to assess a voter’s eligibility, and whether a state registration form is "equivalent" to the federal form.

The brief argued that the Ninth Circuit wrongly concluded a voter’s citizenship attestation on a registration form is sufficient proof of eligibility and improperly interpreted an "equivalent" state form to mean one that is virtually identical to the federal form.

"Once again, far-left activists are using the courts to twist federal law into a straitjacket that prevents states from securing their elections," Jason Snead, executive director of Honest Elections Project, said in a statement to Fox News. "The Honest Elections Project urges the Supreme Court to side with Arizona and preserve the tools states need to ensure that elections are decided only by American citizens."

item.title: GOP lawmaker warns ActBlue 'got caught' as foreign cash probe triggers Fifth Amendment pleas
item.description: Rep. Pat Fallon claims ActBlue operated as a "money laundering operation," alleging millions in foreign donations flowed through the platform.
item.content:encoded:
A top House Republican accused Democratic fundraising powerhouse ActBlue of operating as a "money laundering operation," saying that millions of dollars in foreign contributions had flowed through the platform.

Speaking on the "Fox News Rundown" podcast, Rep. Pat Fallon, R-Texas, said ongoing congressional investigations into the group have uncovered fraud-prevention failures and noted that several people affiliated with ActBlue have invoked the Fifth Amendment while being questioned by lawmakers.

"Well, [it’s clear] ActBlue had become a money laundering operation for the Democratic Party. And that's very unfortunate," Fallon told Fox News' Jessica Rosenthal. "Their compliance and fraud prevention was severely lacking, and they actually were training their employees to do almost no verifications," he added.

TEXAS AG PAXTON SUES DEM FUNDRAISING PLATFORM ACTBLUE, ALLEGING 'FRAUDULENT AND FOREIGN DONATIONS'

Fallon pointed specifically to the platform's past policy of not requiring card verification value, or CVV, codes for some credit card donations, calling it a "huge red flag."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, ActBlue spokesperson De’Andra Roberts LaBoo pushed back against the GOP allegations, saying the investigation is part of a broader political attack.

"President Trump and his allies are engaged in a coordinated campaign of political retaliation and retribution against organizations that they believe threaten them — from universities and law firms to civil rights groups and philanthropies. Now, they’re working to target Democratic fundraising ahead of the midterms," Roberts LaBoo said. 

"ActBlue will not be intimidated, and we refuse to slow down. No other platform does more to protect the integrity of small-dollar democracy — regardless of party. Our platform has raised a record amount of midterm-cycle contributions. With more than a million new donors, Americans are stepping up and fighting back, giving an average contribution of just $36 to the candidates and causes they believe in," she added. 

DEM FUNDRAISING GIANT IN THE HOT SEAT AS GOP LAWMAKERS DEMAND ANSWERS OVER DODGED SUBPOENA

The Committee on House Administration, House Judiciary Committee and House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform are jointly investigating ActBlue's fraud-prevention practices and allegations involving illegal foreign donations.

According to sources familiar with the matter, ActBlue co-founder Matt DeBergalis invoked the Fifth Amendment during a closed-door House deposition. ActBlue board member Kimberly Peeler-Allen also invoked the Fifth Amendment during a separate deposition.

"If they were on the up and up, then why is everyone that used to work for ActBlue taking the Fifth Amendment?" Fallon asked. "Also, why did their entire compliance team leave ActBlue after the 2024 election? I'm talking everybody. Because some shady things were going on, and they got caught with their hand in the cookie jar, and now they're running for the hills."

KEY HOUSE COMMITTEE SCHEDULES HEARING WITH EMBATTLED ACTBLUE CEO: 'NEEDS TO COME CLEAN'

In an April report, the three House committees said ActBlue's entire legal and compliance team had left the platform after the 2024 election.

"Documents produced pursuant to the Committees' subpoenas show the collapse of ActBlue's legal and compliance team in the months after the 2024 election. By March 2025, every member of ActBlue's legal and compliance team resigned, was fired, or went on extended leave from the platform," the committees wrote in April.

ACTBLUE CHIEF HEADS TO CAPITOL HILL HOT SEAT AS DONOR FRAUD PROBE INTENSIFIES

ActBlue later responded to the congressional committees, disputing their findings and denying wrongdoing.

"For three years, ActBlue has been targeted by MAGA Republicans because of who we are and what we stand for, not because of any unlawful conduct. They want to undermine one of democracy’s most powerful tools because they are desperate to hold onto power," the platform said.

HOUSE DEM LASHES OUT AT GOP EFFORTS TO PROBE FOREIGN DONATIONS WITH STUNNING CLAIM ON MOTIVE

ActBlue said it has worked in "good faith" with the investigations and produced thousands of pages of materials, while accusing lawmakers of engaging in "political theater."

ActBlue said it leads the industry in preventing illegal contributions. The group said its fraud-detection system evaluates more than 140 factors and blocks contributions associated with foreign IP addresses, bank accounts and non-U.S. mailing addresses.

ACTBLUE SCRUTINY FUELS NEW GOP BILLS TO TIGHTEN ELECTION DONATION RULES

But Fallon told the "Fox News Rundown" that he believes ActBlue accepted millions of dollars in foreign contributions.

"It’s into the millions. It's hard to say right now. It is vast. And it's definitely game-changing. You can see it reflected in their fundraising numbers now. They're far down from where they were in previous election cycles," Fallon said, adding that he would welcome an investigation by the FBI or other federal agencies.

Fox News Digital’s Elizabeth Elkind and Kelly Phares contributed to this report.

item.title: JD Vance's mother Beverly Vance addresses 'Hillbilly Elegy' movie pay and if a sequel is possible
item.description: Beverly Vance says she refused to accept Hollywood's lowball offer for the "Hillbilly Elegy" film rights, revealing she's happy with her final payout.
item.content:encoded:
Beverly Vance, mother of Vice President J.D. Vance, said she was satisfied with her ultimate payout for the 2020 film adaptation of "Hillbilly Elegy," despite initial attempts by studio executives to lowball her.

Appearing on OutKick’s "Tomi Lahren is Fearless," Beverly Vance addressed the business negotiations surrounding the Netflix movie based on her son’s 2016 bestselling memoir.

The film featured a stacked cast, including Amy Adams portraying Beverly Vance and Glenn Close playing her mother.

VANCE’S MOM FIRES BACK AT EL-SAYED OVER SECOND FAMILY JABS: ‘PROBABLY PUNCH HIM’

"Do you think that you made enough money off of 'Hillbilly Elegy'?" host Tomi Lahren asked. "I know originally they wanted to lowball you."

"Um, I'm happy with what I made," Beverly Vance said.

Lahren pressed further on Hollywood’s standard negotiation tactics, noting that studios often attempt to shortchange individuals selling their life rights. Vance confirmed executives initially tried to pay her less, but acknowledged she refused to accept a low offer.

VANCE UNLOADS ON EL-SAYED AFTER USHA SWIPE WITH BRUTAL WARNING: 'WAY OUT OF YOUR LEAGUE'

"Do you think they thought that you were just gonna just take a little amount and be fine with that? And that wasn't gonna fly with you," Lahren said, pointing out the star power attached to the project.

The discussion also turned to whether the family's story could return to the screen following J.D. Vance's rise to the vice presidency.

When Lahren asked if there should be a "Hillbilly Elegy 2," Vance deferred to her son.

"I think that should probably be J.D.'s decision, since he wrote the book and it's based on his life," Vance said. "That would probably be his call, but whatever he decides, I would be okay with."

For Beverly Vance, a sequel would offer an opportunity to highlight her long-term recovery following the personal addiction struggles depicted in the original movie.

"It would be nice for people to see that I got clean and stayed clean, I think," Vance said.

item.title: MIKE DAVIS: The Trump DOJ should withdraw its statement of interest in the OpenAI lawsuit
item.description: Trump's Justice Department backed OpenAI's fair use argument for AI training on copyrighted works, a move critics say lets Big Tech steal from creators.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump’s Justice Department is the best in modern history — and that is precisely why the MAGA movement must speak up when a proposed policy falls short of the extraordinarily high bar the American people have come to expect of this administration.

The Justice Department recently filed in OpenAI’s private lawsuit a "statement of interest of the United States," arguing Big Tech’s training of massive AI models on copyrighted text constitutes "fair use," largely intended for limited free use of copyrighted materials for educational purposes in classrooms. The Justice Department should withdraw this ill-advised statement.

Essentially, the government’s stated position would let Big Tech oligarchs scrape, copy and commercialize every creative work in America without permission or payment. The government claims this unlimited access is essential for national security, warning any restriction risks losing the AI race to China. That argument is un-American and absurd.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

"We must steal like China to compete against China" is not a principle; it is a surrender of the rule of law. It is especially damaging to the independent creators and conservative media outlets — like Steve Bannon’s War Room, which bypassed legacy gatekeepers, delivered truth directly to the public, and helped elect President Trump both times.

These voices were systematically censored, de-platformed and demonetized by the same Big Tech giants now seeking a free pass to harvest their work. ChatGPT was recently exposed for calling Trump the greatest threat to democracy since Hitler.

Having largely lost the censorship fight, the left and its Big Tech allies are shifting to theft as the new method of control.

Conservatives have long insisted that any serious AI policy must protect the 4Cs: children, communities, conservatives and creators. The latest DOJ policy position fails those. America must win the global AI competition the American way — through markets that respect property rights, not through government-sanctioned expropriation.

AI HAS AN OPINION AND IT USUALLY LEANS LEFT. YOU HAVE A RIGHT TO KNOW ITS AGENDA

Licensing copyrighted material is not a financial burden on an industry spending hundreds of billions annually and enjoying near-limitless capital. Google will still more than thrive if it has to pay — the old-fashioned, American way —the creators it rips off. The creative industry will not survive if Google doesn’t pay.

In a free market, businesses pay for the inputs they need. The music industry already operates this way: Spotify, for example, permits bars, restaurants and other venues to entertain their patrons with others’ music, while the musicians get paid for their work. AI companies can and must do the same.

OPENAI'S SAM ALTMAN WANTS TO NEGOTIATE A 5% STAKE IN COMPANY FOR US IF COMPETITORS AGREE TO KEY PROVISION

President Trump, himself a prolific content creator — as both a bestselling author and television producer — has said it best: "The pioneering spirit of these artists, authors, inventors, and other creators has improved our lives and the lives of millions of people around the world, and will continue to propel us toward a better future." An AI regime that lets companies "train on," or rip off, The Art of the Deal — or any other copyrighted work — without permission is not the art of the deal. It is the art of the steal.

Restricting AI companies’ free use of copyrighted material is simple common sense. The national-security argument offered in its place is a scare tactic designed to short-circuit property right and the rule of law. If these companies were truly worried about national security, they would put their money where their mouth is — redirecting a fraction of their vast wealth to compensate creators rather than ripping them off.

CHINESE ESPIONAGE STEALS $600 BILLION FROM US FIRMS YEARLY. IT’S TIME FOR GOVERNMENT TO ACT

Unlike China, America does not have forced labor. The claim that these Big Tech conglomerates are reliable defenders of American interests is especially laughable. Google, for example, withdrew critical support from the U.S. military’s Project Maven drone program while simultaneously advancing China’s Project Dragonfly — a mass-surveillance and censorship system designed to help the Chinese Communist Party control its own people.

President Trump’s Justice Department should reverse this rare misstep and withdraw its statement of interest in the OpenAI case.

With battle-tested leaders such as Attorney General Todd Blanche, Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, Solicitor General John Sauer, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, and FBI Director Kash Patel, the Trump Justice Department has already done a Herculean job restoring the rule of law after years of weaponization and lawlessness.

Antitrust nominee Adam Candeub, once confirmed, will strengthen that mission further by confronting the Big Tech and other monopolists driving up prices for American consumers.

Because this is the best Justice Department in modern history, the MAGA movement has a duty to insist that its AI policy meets the same high standard. Protect children. Protect communities. Protect conservatives. Protect creators. Let’s win the AI race the American way.

item.title: Well-connected Dem operative learns fate after FBI busts him in child sex abuse sting
item.description: A former Virginia Democratic Party finance chair and 2024 DNC delegate was handed a decade behind bars for child sexual abuse material and other child sex abuse allegations.
item.content:encoded:
A well-connected political consultant in Virginia with ties to the state's Democratic Party was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison after getting caught with child sexual abuse material and attempting to sexually abuse an undercover agent's purported 9-year-old son in an undercover FBI child sex abuse sting.

Randon Sprinkle, 31, of Richmond, was handed the decade-long sentence on Thursday by U.S. District Judge Roderick C. Young following a federal investigation by the FBI’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, according to a Justice Department press release. According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia, Sprinkle was ensnared in a May 2025 undercover operation after making contact on a dating app called Jack'd with an agent posing as the father of a 9-year-old boy.

Authorities said Sprinkle sent the undercover agent a video showing two adults sexually abusing a minor, voiced a desire to travel to Washington, D.C., to abuse the fictitious child, and was later found in possession of dozens of files depicting the sexual abuse of toddlers and infants when agents searched his home.

FBI RAIDS SPANBERGER ALLY OFFICE AS FEDERAL CORRUPTION PROBE TARGETS CANNABIS BUSINESS

Beyond serving as the finance chairman for the Democratic Party of Virginia and the treasurer for the Metro Richmond Area Young Democrats, Sprinkle served as an elected delegate to the 2024 Democratic National Convention, according to public party rosters and local reporting. He also worked as a paid political director for Rep. Jennifer McClellan’s 2021 gubernatorial bid and previously served as her legislative aide when she was a state senator.

Meanwhile, Sprinkle has also worked for other Virginia Democratic Party campaigns, according to consulting payments, including state Sen. Jennifer Boysko.

State campaign finance records compiled by the Virginia Public Access Project (VPAP) also show Sprinkle, who worked as an associate for the Richmond-based Reflex Strategy Group and another consulting group called Alexander Strategies LLC, donated thousands of dollars to the recent statewide campaigns of Rep. Abigail Spanberger and Lt. Gov. Ghazala Hashmi.

Alleged photos preserved online following his arrest show Sprinkle regularly operating alongside national-level Democratic Party politicians as well, including former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, whose name has been floated for a presidential run in 2028, Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, and Spanberger, among others.

Spanberger's transition team previously released a statement after his arrest, thanking the FBI "for their investigative work and for bringing this predator to justice."

"As a former federal law enforcement officer who arrested child predators, she believes that this individual should be swiftly prosecuted and put behind bars for his sickening crimes against children," the statement said. "Upon learning about these appalling reports, the Spanberger campaign immediately donated the full amount of this individual’s prior donations, $1000, to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to support its critical mission of protecting America’s kids."

ILLEGAL ALIEN'S ‘INEXCUSABLE’ CRIME SPARKS INTERSTATE CLASH BETWEEN GOP SEN, DEM GOV: ‘YOU SHOULD BE ASHAMED’

When reached for comment, the Metro Richmond Area Young Democrats referred Fox News Digital to a statement issued by the organization’s executive board following Sprinkle's initial indictment in December 2025, confirming they took "immediate action to terminate all ties."

"The alleged conduct outlined in the indictment is reprehensible, unforgivable, and fundamentally misaligned with the values of our organization," the board said in the statement. "It violates the most basic standards of humanity and decency."

Fox News Digital also reached out to the Democratic Party of Virginia and the public defender representing him but did not hear back in time for publication. .

item.title: Remnants of Henry VIII's long-lost castle found in unexpected location, researcher reveals
item.description: Exclusive photos reveal pieces of King Henry VIII's lost Sandown Castle stonework traced to Dover Castle and Eastry Union Chapel across Kent, a researcher told Fox News Digital.
item.content:encoded:
Pieces of King Henry VIII's long-lost castle were recently found in a somewhat unexpected location: another English castle.

The discovery by researcher Christopher Moore was recently announced by the University of Kent. 

Moore, who specializes in hidden and lost heritage, found evidence that stone used at Dover Castle was taken from Henry VIII's Sandown Castle, a Tudor coastal fortress built roughly 8 miles northeast of Dover that has since been lost to time.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER EERIE ANGLO-SAXON 'SAND BODIES' AT NUCLEAR POWER STATION SITE

Built between 1539 and 1540 to defend the coast of England, Sandown was eventually abandoned and dismantled — and Moore found evidence that some of its stone was reused in a Victorian extension at Constable's Gate at Dover Castle.

Moore traced the stone through historical records and architectural evidence, including an 1883 report documenting materials being sent from Sandown Castle to Dover.

But Dover isn't the only place where pieces of Sandown found a second life.

Moore has identified at least five sites where stone from the lost fortress was reused — and he singled out Eastry Union Chapel in Kent as perhaps the most interesting.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS FIND ARTIFACTS OLDER THAN STONEHENGE BENEATH BRITAIN'S HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT: 'INCREDIBLY RARE'

"It was built for a smaller budget than most of the other examples that I have found that were robbed from Sandown Castle," he told Fox News Digital.

"Due to this, it contained the greatest variety of stonework, which is mainly 'freestones,' [or] stone that can be easily cut."

Exclusive photographs shared with Fox News Digital show Eastry Union Chapel and its Sandown-linked patchwork of stonework.

RARE 1,200-YEAR-OLD CHRISTIAN CROSS FOUND IN FIELD BY METAL DETECTORIST

Moore added that most of the freestones probably came from ruined monasteries, some dating back to Norman England, hundreds of years before the Tudor period.

"Even though Sandown is no longer standing, neither are many of the Norman monasteries that were spoiled to build these Tudor castles," he said.

"That's why Eastry Chapel is so exciting. It likely contains stonework that today has a near 1,000-year history."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Moore also took chemical samples from stone at Eastry and compared them with examples elsewhere in an effort to determine their origins.

The time-consuming process created "a great web of where the masons were likely robbing the stone and where it was going," he noted.

"Essentially, ancient buildings tell such great stories if only we learned to speak their language!" the researcher said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Moore believes many more examples of Sandown's reused masonry remain to be identified.

"I know of at least five sites where stones were taken from Sandown for use elsewhere and [are] still standing today. However, there will be vastly more," Moore said. 

"Sandown did not just fall in the sea."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Moore has also contributed a chapter on Sandown Castle's forgotten history to the recently published book, "Revivalism in Architecture: Referencing and Reworking the Past."

The researcher added that Tudor fortifications were built to be remarkably durable, pointing to Sandown's sister fortress, Deal Castle — which sustained relatively little damage to its original Tudor structure when it was struck by a bomb during World War II.

"For it to fall in the sea is a myth," added Moore. "[Sandown] was systematically robbed through the centuries for a number of uses."
